title: Linking the vault
scenario: The studio links its brand library to the AI app instead of copying files into a vendor. You decide what the link offers and what stays out. Use the exhibit. The plan and the log are made up for this case. The rules come from the docs.
exhibit:
LIBRARY LINK PLAN (made up for this case):
  Server     VaultLink, hosted by the library vendor. Public HTTPS.
  It offers  resources (asset files, found by address). Tools: none yet.
  Folders    PUBLIC, CLIENT-APPROVED, EMBARGOED (next season, unreleased)
  Studio rule  No AI vendor may keep a copy of EMBARGOED files.
  Readers    The studio's app, through the Claude API MCP connector (beta)
             and the OpenAI Responses API.
  Plan B     The files also sit in a Dropbox folder. A teammate suggests
             OpenAI's built-in Dropbox connector (connector_id) with a model
             released in October 2026.

TOOL LIST LOG (made up for this case):
  v1, approved in March:         list_assets, get_asset
  v2, vendor update in September: list_assets, fetch_asset, delete_asset

questions.prompt: VaultLink offers resources only. What happens with the Claude API MCP connector?

options.text: The assets load as before, because resources and tools are the same thing in MCP
options.explanation: They are different. Tools are model-controlled. Resources are application-driven.

options.text: The connector reads them, but only the files in the PUBLIC folder are allowed through
options.explanation: Nothing on the page splits it by folder. The limit is the kind of feature.

options.text: The connector cannot use them, because it supports only tool calls, so ask for tools
options.explanation: Right. Anthropic says only tool calls are currently supported. Test in each place you plan to use the link.

options.text: The connector turns each resource into a copy inside Claude's own file storage by itself
options.explanation: The page describes no such step. It supports tool calls only.

questions.prompt: The log shows v2. delete_asset is new, and get_asset is now fetch_asset. What do you do?

options.text: Accept v2 as it is, because the vendor made the update and so it must be an improvement
options.explanation: Anthropic and OpenAI both warn that a server can change its tools or behaviour at any time.

options.text: Keep only approved read tools on, leave delete_asset off, and test fetch_asset before use
options.explanation: Right. Import only named tools, record the approved list, and test after an update. Anthropic's beta can pin the list.

options.text: Turn every v2 tool on, so that the team can tidy the library from inside the chat window
options.explanation: This gives the AI a new power that nobody approved. Delete is a risk.

options.text: Ignore the log, because tool names are only labels and do not change what the AI can do
options.explanation: A new tool is a new action. A rename can also break a list that names tools.

questions.prompt: Can the EMBARGOED folder go through the Claude connector today?

options.text: Yes, because the connector is covered by zero data retention for all client work
options.explanation: Anthropic says the MCP connector is not covered by ZDR arrangements.

options.text: Yes, if the folder is renamed, since Anthropic only keeps data from named public folders
options.explanation: Anthropic's page does not work by folder names. Data is kept by its standard policy.

options.text: No, keep it out for now, and check retention at the vendor and at the server first
options.explanation: Right. The Claude connector is not ZDR-covered, and the server has its own retention policy. The studio rule forbids outside copies.

options.text: No, because the connector can only ever read files that have already been made public
options.explanation: The connector has no such rule. The issue is who keeps a copy of the data.

questions.prompt: Is OpenAI's built-in Dropbox connector (connector_id) a good base for a model released in October 2026?

options.text: Yes, because built-in connectors are the standard way and are kept for every future model
options.explanation: The page says connector_id is deprecated for models released after September 1, 2026.

options.text: Only if the studio uses Claude, since this deprecation is a rule about Anthropic models
options.explanation: It is OpenAI's own rule, about OpenAI models released after that date.

options.text: Yes, if a person approves each call, since approval removes the deprecation for the model
options.explanation: Approvals control calls. They do not change which models support connector_id.

options.text: No, use server_url for a remote MCP server, or a tunnel for a private one, instead
options.explanation: Right. OpenAI says connector_id is deprecated for models released after September 1, 2026. Existing models keep support.
